170	## Original request
171	
172	# Stockroom
173	
174	I run a small online shop out of a spare room and I keep everything in plain text files: what I sell,
175	what came in and went out of the shelves, and what customers ordered. I'd like a Python tool called
176	**stockroom** that reads those files and answers three questions: what is on the shelves and what
177	needs buying, what an order costs, and what I can ship today. It should work two ways: as a library I
178	can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
179	newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
180	should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.
181	
182	There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
183	**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
184	depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.
185	
186	## The three files
187	
188	They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
189	byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
190	In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
191	whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
192	must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).
193	
194	### `catalog.txt` — what I sell
195	
196	One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:
197	
198	```
199	# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
200	AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
201	cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
202	EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
203	```
204	
205	- **SKU**: two to four letters, a dash, three digits (`AB-100`). Letters in any case are accepted; the
206	  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
207	- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
208	- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
209	  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
210	- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
211	- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
212	  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.
213	
214	### `movements.txt` — what came in and went out
215	
216	One movement per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note
217	is the rest of the line exactly as written, apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.
218	
219	```
220	2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
221	2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
222	2024-03-05 CD-205 40
223	```
224	
225	- **DATE** is `YYYY-MM-DD` and a date that exists (`2024-02-30` is a mistake).
226	- **SKU** must be in the catalogue (any case).
227	- **QUANTITY** is a whole number that is not zero, with an optional sign: positive means stock in,
228	  negative means stock out.
229	- The movements count in date order; movements on the same day keep the order of the file. The
230	  stock of a product may never be below zero at any point in that order. The line that takes it below
231	  zero is the mistake.
232	
233	### `orders.txt` — what customers ordered
234	
235	One order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs:
236	
237	```
238	SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
239	SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
240	```
241	
242	- **ORDER** is `SO-` (any case) and one or more digits, shown in upper case; `SO-7` and `SO-007` are two
243	  different orders. It is unique: a second line with the same order number is a mistake.
244	- **DATE** as above. **CUSTOMER** is one word, shown as typed.
245	- **LINES** is one or more `SKU*QUANTITY` pairs separated by commas, no spaces. The SKU must be in the
246	  catalogue and appear once per order; the quantity is a whole number of one or more (no sign).
247	
248	A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is
249	just empty. A command reads only the files it needs, and a mistake in a file it does not read is not its
250	business: the shelves commands (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`) read the catalogue and the
251	movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and the orders; `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.
252	
253	## Using it as a library
254	
255	```python
256	import stockroom
257	
258	catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt").read())
259	moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt").read(), catalog)
260	print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
261	```
262	
263	- `parse_catalog(text)` returns a `dict` of SKU to a product. A product has `.sku`, `.name`, `.price`
264	  (a `decimal.Decimal`), `.reorder` (an `int`) and `.tax` (`"standard"`, `"reduced"` or `"zero"`).
265	- `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns a list of movements in the order they appear in the text,
266	  each with `.date` (a `datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (an `int`) and `.note` (a `str`, empty when
267	  there is none).
268	- `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns a list of orders in the order they appear, each with `.id`,
269	  `.date`, `.customer` and `.lines`: a list of `(sku, quantity)` pairs in the order written.
270	- A bad line makes any of these raise `stockroom.ParseError`. It is a `ValueError`, its `.line`
271	  attribute is the line number, and its message mentions `line N`.
272	- `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` is a `dict` of SKU to the quantity on the shelf, for every product
273	  in the catalogue (zero when it never moved).
274	- `price_order(order, catalog)` prices a whole order as described under *Prices* and returns a quote with
275	  `.lines` (each with `.sku`, `.quantity`, `.unit`, `.gross`, `.discount`, `.net`), `.subtotal`,
276	  `.order_discount`, `.tax` and `.total`, all `Decimal`s with two decimal places. A discount is zero or
277	  negative.
278	
279	## Prices
280	
281	All of this is exact to the penny and every rounding step rounds halves **up** (`0.005` becomes `0.01`).
282	
283	1. A line's **gross** is its quantity times the unit price.
284	2. A line gets a **volume discount** of 5 % of its gross when the quantity is 10 or more, and 10 % when it
285	   is 50 or more (not both), rounded to the penny. The line's **net** is gross minus that.
286	3. The **subtotal** is the sum of the nets. When it is £500.00 or more the whole order gets an **order
287	   discount** of 3 % of the subtotal, rounded to the penny.
288	4. The order discount is shared out over the lines in proportion to their nets, to the penny: each line's
289	   share is rounded down, and the pennies left over go one each to the lines with the biggest part of a
290	   penny lost (the earlier line first on a tie). A line's **taxable amount** is its net less its share.
291	5. **Tax** is worked out per line on its taxable amount at its product's rate, rounded to the penny, and
292	   added up. Prices do not include tax.
293	6. The **total** is the subtotal, plus the order discount (a negative number), plus the tax.
294	
295	## Using it from the terminal
296	
297	Every command takes `--dir DIR` anywhere on the line (default: the current folder). Options are spelled out in full.
298	
299	```
300	$ stockroom stock
301	AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
302	CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
303	EF-310 0 out Gift voucher
304	
305	$ stockroom quote SO-1001
306	SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme
307	AB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50
308	CD-205 3 1.99 5.97 0.00 5.97
309	subtotal 148.47
310	order discount 0.00
311	tax 28.80
312	total 177.27
313	```
314	
315	**The shelves**
316	
317	- `stockroom stock [--json]` prints one line per product, by SKU: `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` separated by single
318	  spaces. The status is `out` when the stock is zero, `low` when it is above zero and at or under the product's
319	  reorder level, `ok` otherwise.
320	- `stockroom low [--json]` prints one line for each product that is `low` or `out`, by SKU:
321	  `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` where BUY is how many to buy to get back to twice the reorder level, and at least 1
322	  (`max(1, 2 × reorder − onhand)`).
323	- `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints that product's movements, in the order they count, one per
324	  line as `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE`: the quantity with its sign (`+20`, `-3`), the stock after the
325	  movement, and the note (and its space) left out when there is none. A SKU that is not in the catalogue is
326	  refused.
327	- `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` and `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` add a stock-in or
328	  stock-out movement to the end of `movements.txt` (creating it if needed) and print the line they added,
329	  written the way `history` writes a movement without the balance: `DATE SKU ±QUANTITY NOTE`. The quantity is a
330	  whole number of one or more, no sign. I pass the note as a single quoted argument; a note may not contain a
331	  line break. A movement that would break a rule above (an unknown SKU, a quantity that is not a positive
332	  whole number, stock that would go below zero at any point in date order) is refused and the file is left
333	  exactly as it was. If the file does not end in a newline, one is added before the new line.
334	
335	**The orders**
336	
337	- `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` prints the order priced as in the example: a header line
338	  `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER`, one line per order line `SKU QUANTITY UNIT GROSS DISCOUNT NET`, then
339	  `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax` and `total` lines. Amounts have two decimals, discounts carry a minus
340	  sign (zero has none), values are separated by single spaces. An order that is not in `orders.txt` is
341	  refused.
342	- `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` ships what the shelves can cover. For each order line, what is still owed is its
343	  quantity less what earlier shipments of this order sent (the total of the negative quantities for that SKU in movements
344	  whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`, the order number in upper case; capped at the quantity ordered). It ships as many of those as the shelves allow on
345	  DATE: no more than the stock after all movements dated on or before DATE, and no more than the lowest stock at
346	  any later point (so that the shipment never makes a later movement take the stock below zero). It adds one
347	  movement `DATE SKU -N order SO-1001` per line with something to ship, at the end of the file. It prints one
348	  line per order line, `SKU shipped N backordered M` (M is what is still owed afterwards), then
349	  `status open`, `status partial` or `status complete`: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when
350	  nothing has been shipped on any line yet, `partial` otherwise. DATE may not be before the order's date
351	  (refused).
352	- `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` is `quote` for what has actually shipped: the same rules and the same
353	  layout, with the quantities shipped so far (lines with nothing shipped are left out) and `invoice ` in front
354	  of the header line (`invoice SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme`). An order with nothing shipped is refused.
355	- `stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]` has one row per order, by order date and then by order
356	  number: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`: the status as above, the units shipped and
357	  ordered, the quote's total, and the invoice's total (`0.00` when nothing has shipped). `text` is the
358	  default and separates by single spaces. `csv` has the header
359	  `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; `json` is an array of objects with those keys,
360	  the units as numbers and the amounts as strings with two decimals.
361	- With `--json`, `stock` prints an array of `{"sku", "name", "onhand", "status"}`, `low` an array of
362	  `{"sku", "onhand", "reorder", "buy"}`, `history` an array of `{"date", "delta", "balance", "note"}`, and
363	  `quote` / `invoice` an object with `order`, `date`, `customer`, `lines` (objects with `sku`, `quantity`,
364	  `unit`, `gross`, `discount`, `net`), `subtotal`, `order_discount`, `tax` and `total`. Amounts are strings
365	  with two decimals, counts are numbers, except a history `delta`, which is the signed string (`"+20"`, `"-3"`).
366	- `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` take no options except `--dir`: every other argument is taken as typed, so a
367	  dash-led quantity is a bad quantity (refused) and a dash-led note is a note.
368	- The command line is checked first (exit `2` for anything wrong with it), then the files are read, then the
369	  request is carried out.
370	- Exit status: `0` when it worked; `1` when a data file has a mistake or what I asked for is refused (an unknown
371	  SKU or order, a movement that would break a rule, nothing shipped yet), with a message on standard error that
372	  names the file and the line where there is one, and nothing on standard output; `2` when a file cannot be read
373	  (a missing `catalog.txt`, a folder that does not exist, bytes that are not UTF-8) or the command line is wrong
374	  (no command, an unknown command, the wrong number of arguments, an unknown option, a bad option value, a date I
375	  mistyped).
376	- If whatever is reading the output goes away (`stockroom stock | head -1`) it just stops quietly, with status
377	  `0`.

2. As the owner, I run `stockroom low` to see what to buy (back up to twice the reorder level, at least 1).
3. As the owner, I run `stockroom history SKU` to see a product's movements with running balance.
4. As the owner, I run `stockroom receive` / `stockroom ship` to append a movement, and a movement that would break a rule is refused with the file untouched.
5. As the owner, I run `stockroom quote ORDER` to price an order exactly as the Prices rules say.
6. As the owner, I run `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` to ship whatever the shelves can cover, never breaking a later movement.
7. As the owner, I run `stockroom invoice ORDER` to bill what has shipped so far.
8. As the owner, I run `stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]` for an overview of every order.
9. As the owner, when my file has a mistake I'm told the file and line number, exit 1, nothing on stdout.
10. As a scripter, I `import stockroom` and use `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements`, `parse_orders`, `stock_levels`, `price_order`, `ParseError`.

can `import stockroom` from my own scripts, and as a `stockroom` command in the terminal. Python 3.9 or
newer, standard library only (no third-party packages). Running `pip install .` in the project folder
should give me both the importable library and the `stockroom` command.

There are two halves to it: the **shelves** (the catalogue, the stock movements, what is low) and the
**orders** (prices, discounts, tax, shipping what is in stock, invoices, a report). The orders half
depends on the shelves, so build them in that order.

## The three files

They live in one folder (the command's current folder, or the one named by `--dir`). Text is UTF-8; a
byte order mark at the start of a file is ignored; a line ends at LF or at CRLF and nowhere else.
In every file, blank lines are ignored, and so are lines starting with `#` (after any leading
whitespace). Anything else that does not follow the rules below is a mistake in my file, and the tool
must tell me which file and which line (counting from 1, blank and comment lines included).

### `catalog.txt` — what I sell

One product per line, fields separated by `|`, whitespace around each field trimmed:

```
# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
```

- **SKU**: two to four letters, a dash, three digits (`AB-100`). Letters in any case are accepted; the
  SKU is always shown in upper case. Two lines with the same SKU are a mistake.
- **name**: not empty. It may contain anything except `|`.
- **price**: in pounds, at least `0.01`, at most two decimal places (`12`, `12.5`, `1.99` are fine;
  `12.505`, `1,000.00`, `-3` and `abc` are not).
- **reorder**: the stock level at or under which I need to buy more: a whole number, zero or more.
- **tax** (optional, `standard` when the field is left out, so a line has four or five fields): one of
  `standard` (20 %), `reduced` (5 %) or `zero` (0 %), in any case.

### `movements.txt` — what came in and went out

One movement per line: `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs. The note
is the rest of the line exactly as written, apart from trimming whitespace at both ends.

```
2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
```

- **DATE** is `YYYY-MM-DD` and a date that exists (`2024-02-30` is a mistake).
- **SKU** must be in the catalogue (any case).
- **QUANTITY** is a whole number that is not zero, with an optional sign: positive means stock in,
  negative means stock out.
- The movements count in date order; movements on the same day keep the order of the file. The
  stock of a product may never be below zero at any point in that order. The line that takes it below
  zero is the mistake.

### `orders.txt` — what customers ordered

One order per line: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER LINES`, separated by any amount of spaces or tabs:

```
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
```

- **ORDER** is `SO-` (any case) and one or more digits, shown in upper case; `SO-7` and `SO-007` are two
  different orders. It is unique: a second line with the same order number is a mistake.
- **DATE** as above. **CUSTOMER** is one word, shown as typed.
- **LINES** is one or more `SKU*QUANTITY` pairs separated by commas, no spaces. The SKU must be in the
  catalogue and appear once per order; the quantity is a whole number of one or more (no sign).

A missing `catalog.txt` is an error for every command. A missing `movements.txt` or `orders.txt` is
just empty. A command reads only the files it needs, and a mistake in a file it does not read is not its
business: the shelves commands (`stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`) read the catalogue and the
movements; `quote` reads the catalogue and the orders; `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report` read all three.

## Using it as a library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
```

- `parse_catalog(text)` returns a `dict` of SKU to a product. A product has `.sku`, `.name`, `.price`
  (a `decimal.Decimal`), `.reorder` (an `int`) and `.tax` (`"standard"`, `"reduced"` or `"zero"`).
- `parse_movements(text, catalog)` returns a list of movements in the order they appear in the text,
  each with `.date` (a `datetime.date`), `.sku`, `.quantity` (an `int`) and `.note` (a `str`, empty when
  there is none).
- `parse_orders(text, catalog)` returns a list of orders in the order they appear, each with `.id`,
  `.date`, `.customer` and `.lines`: a list of `(sku, quantity)` pairs in the order written.
- A bad line makes any of these raise `stockroom.ParseError`. It is a `ValueError`, its `.line`
  attribute is the line number, and its message mentions `line N`.
- `stock_levels(catalog, movements)` is a `dict` of SKU to the quantity on the shelf, for every product
  in the catalogue (zero when it never moved).
- `price_order(order, catalog)` prices a whole order as described under *Prices* and returns a quote with
  `.lines` (each with `.sku`, `.quantity`, `.unit`, `.gross`, `.discount`, `.net`), `.subtotal`,
  `.order_discount`, `.tax` and `.total`, all `Decimal`s with two decimal places. A discount is zero or
  negative.

## Prices

All of this is exact to the penny and every rounding step rounds halves **up** (`0.005` becomes `0.01`).

1. A line's **gross** is its quantity times the unit price.
2. A line gets a **volume discount** of 5 % of its gross when the quantity is 10 or more, and 10 % when it
   is 50 or more (not both), rounded to the penny. The line's **net** is gross minus that.
3. The **subtotal** is the sum of the nets. When it is £500.00 or more the whole order gets an **order
   discount** of 3 % of the subtotal, rounded to the penny.
4. The order discount is shared out over the lines in proportion to their nets, to the penny: each line's
   share is rounded down, and the pennies left over go one each to the lines with the biggest part of a
   penny lost (the earlier line first on a tie). A line's **taxable amount** is its net less its share.
5. **Tax** is worked out per line on its taxable amount at its product's rate, rounded to the penny, and
   added up. Prices do not include tax.
6. The **total** is the subtotal, plus the order discount (a negative number), plus the tax.

## Using it from the terminal

Every command takes `--dir DIR` anywhere on the line (default: the current folder). Options are spelled out in full.

```
$ stockroom stock
AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome
CD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix
EF-310 0 out Gift voucher

$ stockroom quote SO-1001
SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme
AB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50
CD-205 3 1.99 5.97 0.00 5.97
subtotal 148.47
order discount 0.00
tax 28.80
total 177.27
```

**The shelves**

- `stockroom stock [--json]` prints one line per product, by SKU: `SKU ONHAND STATUS NAME` separated by single
  spaces. The status is `out` when the stock is zero, `low` when it is above zero and at or under the product's
  reorder level, `ok` otherwise.
- `stockroom low [--json]` prints one line for each product that is `low` or `out`, by SKU:
  `SKU ONHAND REORDER BUY` where BUY is how many to buy to get back to twice the reorder level, and at least 1
  (`max(1, 2 × reorder − onhand)`).
- `stockroom history SKU [--json]` prints that product's movements, in the order they count, one per
  line as `DATE DELTA BALANCE NOTE`: the quantity with its sign (`+20`, `-3`), the stock after the
  movement, and the note (and its space) left out when there is none. A SKU that is not in the catalogue is
  refused.
- `stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` and `stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]` add a stock-in or
  stock-out movement to the end of `movements.txt` (creating it if needed) and print the line they added,
  written the way `history` writes a movement without the balance: `DATE SKU ±QUANTITY NOTE`. The quantity is a
  whole number of one or more, no sign. I pass the note as a single quoted argument; a note may not contain a
  line break. A movement that would break a rule above (an unknown SKU, a quantity that is not a positive
  whole number, stock that would go below zero at any point in date order) is refused and the file is left
  exactly as it was. If the file does not end in a newline, one is added before the new line.

**The orders**

- `stockroom quote ORDER [--json]` prints the order priced as in the example: a header line
  `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER`, one line per order line `SKU QUANTITY UNIT GROSS DISCOUNT NET`, then
  `subtotal`, `order discount`, `tax` and `total` lines. Amounts have two decimals, discounts carry a minus
  sign (zero has none), values are separated by single spaces. An order that is not in `orders.txt` is
  refused.
- `stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE` ships what the shelves can cover. For each order line, what is still owed is its
  quantity less what earlier shipments of this order sent (the total of the negative quantities for that SKU in movements
  whose note is exactly `order SO-1001`, the order number in upper case; capped at the quantity ordered). It ships as many of those as the shelves allow on
  DATE: no more than the stock after all movements dated on or before DATE, and no more than the lowest stock at
  any later point (so that the shipment never makes a later movement take the stock below zero). It adds one
  movement `DATE SKU -N order SO-1001` per line with something to ship, at the end of the file. It prints one
  line per order line, `SKU shipped N backordered M` (M is what is still owed afterwards), then
  `status open`, `status partial` or `status complete`: `complete` when nothing is owed on any line, `open` when
  nothing has been shipped on any line yet, `partial` otherwise. DATE may not be before the order's date
  (refused).
- `stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]` is `quote` for what has actually shipped: the same rules and the same
  layout, with the quantities shipped so far (lines with nothing shipped are left out) and `invoice ` in front
  of the header line (`invoice SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme`). An order with nothing shipped is refused.
- `stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]` has one row per order, by order date and then by order
  number: `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER STATUS SHIPPED/ORDERED QUOTED INVOICED`: the status as above, the units shipped and
  ordered, the quote's total, and the invoice's total (`0.00` when nothing has shipped). `text` is the
  default and separates by single spaces. `csv` has the header
  `order,date,customer,status,ordered,shipped,quoted,invoiced`; `json` is an array of objects with those keys,
  the units as numbers and the amounts as strings with two decimals.
- With `--json`, `stock` prints an array of `{"sku", "name", "onhand", "status"}`, `low` an array of
  `{"sku", "onhand", "reorder", "buy"}`, `history` an array of `{"date", "delta", "balance", "note"}`, and
  `quote` / `invoice` an object with `order`, `date`, `customer`, `lines` (objects with `sku`, `quantity`,
  `unit`, `gross`, `discount`, `net`), `subtotal`, `order_discount`, `tax` and `total`. Amounts are strings
  with two decimals, counts are numbers, except a history `delta`, which is the signed string (`"+20"`, `"-3"`).
- `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` take no options except `--dir`: every other argument is taken as typed, so a
  dash-led quantity is a bad quantity (refused) and a dash-led note is a note.
- The command line is checked first (exit `2` for anything wrong with it), then the files are read, then the
  request is carried out.
- Exit status: `0` when it worked; `1` when a data file has a mistake or what I asked for is refused (an unknown
  SKU or order, a movement that would break a rule, nothing shipped yet), with a message on standard error that

import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

if SRC not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SRC)

CATALOG = """# SKU   | name            | price | reorder | tax
AB-100 | Garden gnome     | 12.50 | 5       | standard
cd-205 | Seed packet, mix | 1.99  | 40      | reduced
EF-310 | Gift voucher     | 25.00 | 0
"""

MOVEMENTS = """2024-03-01 AB-100 +20 first delivery
2024-03-04 ab-100 -3 order SO-1001
2024-03-05 CD-205 40
"""

ORDERS = """SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme AB-100*12,CD-205*3
SO-1002 2024-03-09 Bea ab-100*2
"""


def run_cli(args, cwd=None, input_bytes=None):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = SRC + os.pathsep + env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
    env.pop("PYTHONIOENCODING", None)
    env["LC_ALL"] = "C"
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "stockroom"] + list(args), cwd=cwd, env=env,
                          input=input_bytes, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)


class TempShop:
    """A temporary folder holding the three files."""

    def __init__(self, catalog=CATALOG, movements=MOVEMENTS, orders=ORDERS):
        self._tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.dir = self._tmp.name
        for name, text in (("catalog.txt", catalog), ("movements.txt", movements), ("orders.txt", orders)):
            if text is not None:
                self.write(name, text)

    def path(self, name):
        return os.path.join(self.dir, name)

    def write(self, name, text):
        data = text if isinstance(text, bytes) else text.encode("utf-8")
        with open(self.path(name), "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(data)

    def read(self, name):
        with open(self.path(name), "rb") as handle:
            return handle.read()

    def run(self, *args):
        return run_cli(["--dir", self.dir] + list(args))

    def cleanup(self):
        self._tmp.cleanup()

import datetime
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

import support  # noqa: F401  (puts src on sys.path)

import stockroom
from stockroom import ParseError, parse_catalog, parse_movements, parse_orders, stock_levels


def catalog():
    return parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)


class LineReadingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_bom_crlf_comments_and_blank_lines(self):
        text = "﻿# header\r\n\r\n   # indented comment\r\n\t \r\nab-100 | Gnome | 1 | 0\r\n"
        cat = parse_catalog(text)
        self.assertEqual(list(cat), ["AB-100"])
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-100"].name, "Gnome")

    def test_line_numbers_count_blank_and_comment_lines(self):
        text = "# c\n\nAB-100 | x | 1 | 0\n   \nbad line\n"
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_catalog(text)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 5)
        self.assertIn("line 5", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_only_lf_and_crlf_end_lines(self):
        # Characters str.splitlines() would split on must not end a line.
        for sep in [" ", "\x0b", "\x0c", "\x1c", "\x85", "\r"]:
            with self.subTest(sep=repr(sep)):
                text = f"AB-100 | Gnome | 1 | 0{sep}CD-205 | Seed | 2 | 0\n"
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse_catalog(text)
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 1)

    def test_separator_inside_name_is_kept(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("AB-100 | Gnome big | 1 | 0\n")
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-100"].name, "Gnome big")

    def test_parse_error_is_value_error(self):
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(ParseError, ValueError))
        self.assertIs(stockroom.ParseError, ParseError)


class CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example(self):
        cat = catalog()
        self.assertEqual(list(cat), ["AB-100", "CD-205", "EF-310"])
        p = cat["CD-205"]
        self.assertEqual((p.sku, p.name, p.price, p.reorder, p.tax),
                         ("CD-205", "Seed packet, mix", Decimal("1.99"), 40, "reduced"))
        self.assertIsInstance(p.price, Decimal)
        self.assertIsInstance(p.reorder, int)
        self.assertEqual(cat["EF-310"].tax, "standard")
        self.assertEqual(str(cat["EF-310"].price), "25.00")

    def test_good_values(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("abcd-001|N|12|0|ZERO\nAb-002 | N | 12.5 | 3 | Reduced\nXY-003|N|0.01|1|standard\n")
        self.assertEqual(cat["ABCD-001"].price, Decimal("12.00"))
        self.assertEqual(cat["ABCD-001"].tax, "zero")
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-002"].price, Decimal("12.50"))
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-002"].tax, "reduced")
        self.assertEqual(cat["XY-003"].price, Decimal("0.01"))

    def test_bad_lines(self):
        bad = {
            "A-100 | x | 1 | 0": "sku one letter",
            "ABCDE-100 | x | 1 | 0": "sku five letters",
            "AB-10 | x | 1 | 0": "sku two digits",
            "AB-1000 | x | 1 | 0": "sku four digits",
            "AB100 | x | 1 | 0": "no dash",
            "ÄB-100 | x | 1 | 0": "non-ascii letter",
            "AB-١٠٠ | x | 1 | 0": "unicode digits",
            "AB-100 |  | 1 | 0": "empty name",
            "AB-100 | x | 12.505 | 0": "three decimals",
            "AB-100 | x | 1,000.00 | 0": "comma",
            "AB-100 | x | -3 | 0": "negative",
            "AB-100 | x | abc | 0": "abc",
            "AB-100 | x | 0 | 0": "zero price",
            "AB-100 | x | 0.00 | 0": "zero price decimals",
            "AB-100 | x | 12. | 0": "trailing dot",
            "AB-100 | x | .5 | 0": "leading dot",
            "AB-100 | x | +1 | 0": "plus",
            "AB-100 | x | 1e2 | 0": "exponent",
            "AB-100 | x | NaN | 0": "nan",
            "AB-100 | x | 1_000 | 0": "underscore price",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | -1": "negative reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 1_0": "underscore reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | ٣": "unicode reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 1.5": "fraction reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 0 | luxury": "bad tax",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 0 | ": "empty tax",
            "AB-100 | x | 1": "three fields",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 0 | zero | more": "six fields",
        }
        for line, why in bad.items():
            with self.subTest(why=why):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse_catalog("# ok\n" + line + "\n")
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 2)

    def test_duplicate_sku_any_case_second_line(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_catalog("AB-100|x|1|0\n\nab-100|y|1|0\n")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 3)


class MovementTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example(self):
        moves = parse_movements(support.MOVEMENTS, catalog())
        self.assertEqual(len(moves), 3)
        m = moves[1]
        self.assertEqual((m.date, m.sku, m.quantity, m.note),
                         (datetime.date(2024, 3, 4), "AB-100", -3, "order SO-1001"))
        self.assertEqual(moves[2].note, "")
        self.assertEqual(moves[2].quantity, 40)

    def test_note_kept_as_written(self):
        moves = parse_movements("2024-03-01\tAB-100   +5 \t a  b\tc  \t\n", catalog())
        self.assertEqual(moves[0].note, "a  b\tc")

    def test_bad_lines(self):
        bad = {
            "2024-02-30 AB-100 5": "no such date",
            "2024-3-01 AB-100 5": "short month",
            "24-03-01 AB-100 5": "short year",
            "2024-03-01 ZZ-999 5": "unknown sku",
            "2024-03-01 AB100 5": "bad sku",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 0": "zero",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 -0": "minus zero",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 +0": "plus zero",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 1.5": "fraction",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 1_0": "underscore",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 ٥": "unicode digit",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100": "two tokens",
            "2024-03-01 AB-100 ++5": "double sign",
        }
        for line, why in bad.items():
            with self.subTest(why=why):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse_movements("\n" + line + "\n", catalog())
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 2)

    def test_below_zero_in_date_order(self):
        # The file is out of date order; the later-dated delivery does not help.
        text = "2024-03-05 AB-100 +5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 -2\n"
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_movements(text, catalog())
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 2)

    def test_same_day_keeps_file_order(self):
        cat = catalog()
        parse_movements("2024-03-01 AB-100 +5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 -5\n", cat)
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_movements("2024-03-01 AB-100 -5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 +5\n", cat)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 1)

    def test_returns_file_order(self):
        moves = parse_movements("2024-03-05 AB-100 +5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 +2\n", catalog())
        self.assertEqual([m.quantity for m in moves], [5, 2])


class OrderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_example(self):
        orders = parse_orders(support.ORDERS, catalog())
        self.assertEqual([o.id for o in orders], ["SO-1001", "SO-1002"])
        o = orders[0]
        self.assertEqual(o.date, datetime.date(2024, 3, 3))
        self.assertEqual(o.customer, "acme")
        self.assertEqual(o.lines, [("AB-100", 12), ("CD-205", 3)])
        self.assertEqual(orders[1].lines, [("AB-100", 2)])

    def test_id_upper_case_and_leading_zeros_distinct(self):
        orders = parse_orders("so-7 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1\nSO-007 2024-01-01 b AB-100*1\n", catalog())
        self.assertEqual([o.id for o in orders], ["SO-7", "SO-007"])

    def test_bad_lines(self):
        bad = {
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a": "three tokens",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1 extra": "five tokens",
            "SX-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1": "bad prefix",
            "SO- 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1": "no digits",
            "SO-1 2024-13-01 a AB-100*1": "bad date",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a ZZ-999*1": "unknown sku",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*0": "zero qty",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*+1": "signed qty",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1,": "empty pair",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100": "no star",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1*2": "two stars",
            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1,ab-100*2": "repeated sku",
        }
        for line, why in bad.items():
            with self.subTest(why=why):
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse_orders("# c\n" + line + "\n", catalog())
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 2)

    def test_duplicate_order_second_line(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_orders("SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1\nso-1 2024-01-02 b AB-100*1\n", catalog())
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 2)


class StockLevelTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_product(self):
        cat = catalog()
        moves = parse_movements(support.MOVEMENTS, cat)
        self.assertEqual(stock_levels(cat, moves), {"AB-100": 17, "CD-205": 40, "EF-310": 0})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

D = Decimal


class PriceOrderTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_request_example_so_1001(self):
        cat = parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)
        order = parse_orders(support.ORDERS, cat)[0]
        q = price_order(order, cat)
        self.assertEqual([(l.sku, l.quantity, l.unit, l.gross, l.discount, l.net) for l in q.lines], [
            ("AB-100", 12, D("12.50"), D("150.00"), D("-7.50"), D("142.50")),
            ("CD-205", 3, D("1.99"), D("5.97"), D("0.00"), D("5.97")),
        ])
        self.assertEqual((q.subtotal, q.order_discount, q.tax, q.total),
                         (D("148.47"), D("0.00"), D("28.80"), D("177.27")))
        self.assertEqual(str(q.lines[1].discount), "0.00")
        self.assertEqual(str(q.order_discount), "0.00")

    def test_volume_discount_bands_and_half_up(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("AA-001|x|0.25|0|zero\nBB-002|x|0.50|0|reduced\nCC-003|x|1|0|zero\n")

        class O:
            lines = [("AA-001", 10), ("BB-002", 1), ("CC-003", 50)]

        q = price_order(O, cat)
        # 2.50 * 5% = 0.125 -> 0.13 (half up)
        self.assertEqual(q.lines[0].discount, D("-0.13"))
        self.assertEqual(q.lines[0].net, D("2.37"))
        # 50 or more: 10%, not both
        self.assertEqual(q.lines[2].discount, D("-5.00"))
        # tax 0.50 * 5% = 0.025 -> 0.03 (half up)
        self.assertEqual(q.tax, D("0.03"))
        self.assertEqual(q.lines[1].discount, D("0.00"))

    def test_order_discount_and_allocation(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("AA-001|x|170.12|0|standard\nBB-002|x|170.12|0|reduced\nCC-003|x|170.12|0|zero\n")
        order = parse_orders("SO-1 2024-01-01 a AA-001*1,BB-002*1,CC-003*1\n", cat)[0]
        q = price_order(order, cat)
        self.assertEqual(q.subtotal, D("510.36"))
        self.assertEqual(q.order_discount, D("-15.31"))
        # shares 5.11, 5.10, 5.10 -> tax 33.00 + 8.25 + 0
        self.assertEqual(q.tax, D("41.25"))
        self.assertEqual(q.total, D("536.30"))

    def test_order_discount_half_up_with_volume(self):
        cat = parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)
        order = parse_orders("SO-9 2024-01-01 a AB-100*50\n", cat)[0]
        q = price_order(order, cat)
        self.assertEqual(q.lines[0].net, D("562.50"))
        self.assertEqual(q.order_discount, D("-16.88"))
        self.assertEqual(q.tax, D("109.12"))
        self.assertEqual(q.total, D("654.74"))

    def test_threshold_is_inclusive(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("AA-001|x|500|0|zero\nBB-002|x|499.99|0|zero\n")
        at = parse_orders("SO-1 2024-01-01 a AA-001*1\nSO-2 2024-01-01 a BB-002*1\n", cat)
        self.assertEqual(price_order(at[0], cat).order_discount, D("-15.00"))
        self.assertEqual(price_order(at[1], cat).order_discount, D("0.00"))


class AllocateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_tie_goes_to_earlier_line(self):
        self.assertEqual(allocate(1531, [17012, 17012, 17012]), [511, 510, 510])

    def test_largest_remainder_wins(self):
        # 1500*25001/50001 = 750.015, 1500*25000/50001 = 749.985
        self.assertEqual(allocate(1500, [25001, 25000]), [750, 750])
        self.assertEqual(allocate(10, [1, 1, 1]), [4, 3, 3])
        self.assertEqual(allocate(5, [1, 2]), [2, 3])

    def test_zero(self):
        self.assertEqual(allocate(0, [5, 6]), [0, 0])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

from decimal import Decimal

import support  # noqa: F401  (puts src on sys.path)

import stockroom

def catalog():
    return parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)


class LineReadingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_bom_crlf_comments_and_blank_lines(self):
        text = "\ufeff# header\r\n\r\n   # indented comment\r\n\t \r\nab-100 | Gnome | 1 | 0\r\n"
        cat = parse_catalog(text)
        self.assertEqual(list(cat), ["AB-100"])
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-100"].name, "Gnome")

    def test_line_numbers_count_blank_and_comment_lines(self):
        text = "# c\n\nAB-100 | x | 1 | 0\n   \nbad line\n"
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_catalog(text)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 5)
        self.assertIn("line 5", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_only_lf_and_crlf_end_lines(self):
        # Characters str.splitlines() would split on must not end a line.
        for sep in ["\u2028", "\x0b", "\x0c", "\x1c", "\x85", "\r"]:
            with self.subTest(sep=repr(sep)):
                text = f"AB-100 | Gnome | 1 | 0{sep}CD-205 | Seed | 2 | 0\n"
                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
                    parse_catalog(text)
                self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 1)

    def test_separator_inside_name_is_kept(self):
        cat = parse_catalog("AB-100 | Gnome\u2028big | 1 | 0\n")
        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-100"].name, "Gnome\u2028big")

    def test_parse_error_is_value_error(self):
        self.assertTrue(issubclass(ParseError, ValueError))
        self.assertIs(stockroom.ParseError, ParseError)

        self.assertEqual(cat["ABCD-001"].price, Decimal("12.00"))
        self.assertEqual(cat["ABCD-001"].tax, "zero")

        self.assertEqual(cat["AB-002"].tax, "reduced")

        bad = {
            "A-100 | x | 1 | 0": "sku one letter",

            "AB-100 | x | 0 | 0": "zero price",

            "AB-100 | x | +1 | 0": "plus",
            "AB-100 | x | 1e2 | 0": "exponent",
            "AB-100 | x | NaN | 0": "nan",
            "AB-100 | x | 1_000 | 0": "underscore price",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | -1": "negative reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 1_0": "underscore reorder",
            "AB-100 | x | 1 | ٣": "unicode reorder",

            "AB-100 | x | 1 | 0 | ": "empty tax",

        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 3)


class MovementTests(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_same_day_keeps_file_order(self):
        cat = catalog()

        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:
            parse_movements("2024-03-01 AB-100 -5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 +5\n", cat)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.line, 1)

    def test_returns_file_order(self):
        moves = parse_movements("2024-03-05 AB-100 +5\n2024-03-01 AB-100 +2\n", catalog())
        self.assertEqual([m.quantity for m in moves], [5, 2])


class OrderTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.assertEqual([o.id for o in orders], ["SO-1001", "SO-1002"])

    def test_bad_lines(self):
        bad = {

            "SO-1 2024-01-01 a AB-100*1 extra": "five tokens",

                with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:

    def test_duplicate_order_second_line(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ParseError) as ctx:

class StockLevelTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_product(self):

import json

import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

import support
from support import TempShop, run_cli


class CliCase(unittest.TestCase):
    catalog = support.CATALOG
    movements = support.MOVEMENTS
    orders = support.ORDERS

    def setUp(self):
        self.shop = TempShop(self.catalog, self.movements, self.orders)
        self.addCleanup(self.shop.cleanup)

    def ok(self, *args):
        r = self.shop.run(*args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr.decode())
        self.assertEqual(r.stderr, b"")
        return r.stdout.decode("utf-8")

    def fails(self, status, *args, contains=()):
        r = self.shop.run(*args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, status, (r.stdout, r.stderr))
        self.assertEqual(r.stdout, b"")
        err = r.stderr.decode("utf-8")
        self.assertTrue(err.strip())
        for text in contains:
            self.assertIn(text, err)
        return err


class ShelvesTests(CliCase):
    def test_stock(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("stock"),
                         "AB-100 17 ok Garden gnome\nCD-205 40 low Seed packet, mix\nEF-310 0 out Gift voucher\n")

    def test_stock_json(self):
        data = json.loads(self.ok("stock", "--json"))
        self.assertEqual(data[0], {"sku": "AB-100", "name": "Garden gnome", "onhand": 17, "status": "ok"})
        self.assertEqual(list(data[0]), ["sku", "name", "onhand", "status"])
        self.assertEqual(len(data), 3)

        r = run_cli(["--json", "stock", "--dir", self.shop.dir])
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0)
        self.assertEqual(len(json.loads(r.stdout)), 3)
        r = run_cli(["stock", f"--dir={self.shop.dir}"])
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0)

    def test_dir_default_is_current_folder(self):
        r = run_cli(["stock"], cwd=self.shop.dir)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0)
        self.assertTrue(r.stdout.startswith(b"AB-100 17 ok"))

    def test_low(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("low"), "CD-205 40 40 40\nEF-310 0 0 1\n")
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.ok("low", "--json"))[1],
                         {"sku": "EF-310", "onhand": 0, "reorder": 0, "buy": 1})

    def test_history(self):
        self.shop.write("movements.txt", support.MOVEMENTS + "2024-02-01 AB-100 +1\n")
        self.assertEqual(self.ok("history", "ab-100"),
                         "2024-02-01 +1 1\n2024-03-01 +20 21 first delivery\n2024-03-04 -3 18 order SO-1001\n")
        data = json.loads(self.ok("history", "AB-100", "--json"))

        self.assertEqual(self.ok("ship", "2024-03-07", "EF-310", "1"), "2024-03-07 EF-310 -1\n")

class CliCase(unittest.TestCase):
    catalog = support.CATALOG
    movements = support.MOVEMENTS
    orders = support.ORDERS

    def setUp(self):
        self.shop = TempShop(self.catalog, self.movements, self.orders)
        self.addCleanup(self.shop.cleanup)

    def ok(self, *args):
        r = self.shop.run(*args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, 0, r.stderr.decode())
        self.assertEqual(r.stderr, b"")
        return r.stdout.decode("utf-8")

    def fails(self, status, *args, contains=()):
        r = self.shop.run(*args)
        self.assertEqual(r.returncode, status, (r.stdout, r.stderr))
        self.assertEqual(r.stdout, b"")
        err = r.stderr.decode("utf-8")
        self.assertTrue(err.strip())
        for text in contains:
            self.assertIn(text, err)
        return err

# .rtdd/config.yaml — written by `rtdd init`. Every list is globs over
# repo-relative paths; a key you set replaces its default wholesale.
# See docs/specs/2026-10-07-node-graph.md §4.1, §5 and §6.

# Files the scanner never reads.
scan_exclude:
  - "vendor/**"
  - "node_modules/**"
  - "third_party/**"
  - "**/*.min.js"
  - "dist/**"
  - "build/**"
  - ".rtdd/**"
  - "graphify-out/**"

# Files read for their file node and the paths they name, never for definitions.
definition_exclude:
  - "**/*.md"
  - "**/*.mdc"
  - "**/*.markdown"
  - "**/*.rst"
  - "**/*.txt"
  - "**/*.adoc"

# A function, method or test in a matching file is a test.
test_files:
  - "**/test_*"
  - "**/*_test.*"
  - "**/*.test.*"
  - "**/*.spec.*"
  - "**/*Test.*"
  - "**/*Tests.*"
  - "**/tests/**"
  - "**/test/**"
  - "**/spec/**"
  - "**/__tests__/**"

# A matching file is never a test file, whatever test_files says.
test_exclude:
  - "**/testdata/**"
  - "**/fixtures/**"

# A matching test file runs only as a whole: its functions are helpers, its path is the test.
whole_file_tests:
  - "**/test_*.sh"
  - "**/*_test.sh"
  - "**/*.bats"

# graphify's graph, used when this file exists. rtdd never runs graphify.
graphify_path: "graphify-out/graph.json"

import datetime
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

import support  # noqa: F401  (puts src on sys.path)

from stockroom import cli, parse_catalog, parse_movements, parse_orders
from stockroom.orders import (
    available_on,
    fulfil_plan,
    invoice_quote,
    order_note,
    order_status,
    report_rows,
    shipped_so_far,
)
from stockroom.parsing import ParseError, counting_order
from stockroom.pricing import fmt, money

D = Decimal


def shop(movements=support.MOVEMENTS):
    cat = parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)
    return cat, parse_movements(movements, cat), parse_orders(support.ORDERS, cat)


class OrderLogicTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_order_note(self):
        _, _, orders = shop()
        self.assertEqual(order_note(orders[0]), "order SO-1001")

    def test_shipped_so_far_matches_exact_note_and_caps(self):
        moves_text = (support.MOVEMENTS + "2024-03-05 AB-100 -1 order so-1001\n"
                      "2024-03-05 AB-100 -1 order SO-1001 extra\n2024-03-05 CD-205 -30 order SO-1001\n")
        _, moves, orders = shop(moves_text)
        self.assertEqual(shipped_so_far(orders[0], moves), {"AB-100": 3, "CD-205": 3})

    def test_order_status(self):
        _, _, orders = shop()
        o = orders[0]
        self.assertEqual(order_status(o, {"AB-100": 0, "CD-205": 0}), "open")
        self.assertEqual(order_status(o, {"AB-100": 1, "CD-205": 0}), "partial")
        self.assertEqual(order_status(o, {"AB-100": 12, "CD-205": 3}), "complete")

    def test_available_on(self):
        cat = parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)
        moves = parse_movements("2024-03-01 AB-100 +20\n2024-03-10 AB-100 -15\n2024-03-12 AB-100 +5\n"
                                "2024-03-12 AB-100 -8\n", cat)
        self.assertEqual(available_on("AB-100", datetime.date(2024, 2, 1), moves), 0)
        self.assertEqual(available_on("AB-100", datetime.date(2024, 3, 5), moves), 2)
        self.assertEqual(available_on("AB-100", datetime.date(2024, 3, 10), moves), 2)
        self.assertEqual(available_on("AB-100", datetime.date(2024, 3, 12), moves), 2)
        self.assertEqual(available_on("CD-205", datetime.date(2024, 3, 12), moves), 0)

    def test_fulfil_plan(self):
        _, moves, orders = shop()
        self.assertEqual(fulfil_plan(orders[0], datetime.date(2024, 3, 4), moves), {"AB-100": 9, "CD-205": 0})
        self.assertEqual(fulfil_plan(orders[0], datetime.date(2024, 3, 5), moves), {"AB-100": 9, "CD-205": 3})

    def test_invoice_quote(self):
        cat, moves, orders = shop()
        q = invoice_quote(orders[0], cat, moves)
        self.assertEqual([(l.sku, l.quantity) for l in q.lines], [("AB-100", 3)])
        self.assertEqual(q.total, D("45.00"))
        self.assertIsNone(invoice_quote(orders[1], cat, moves))

    def test_report_rows_sorted(self):
        cat, moves, _ = shop()
        orders = parse_orders("SO-20 2024-03-02 b AB-100*1\nSO-3 2024-03-02 a AB-100*1\n"
                              "SO-003 2024-03-02 c AB-100*1\nSO-1 2024-03-03 d AB-100*1\n", cat)
        rows = report_rows(orders, cat, moves)
        self.assertEqual([r["order"] for r in rows], ["SO-003", "SO-3", "SO-20", "SO-1"])
        self.assertEqual(rows[0]["invoiced"], None)
        self.assertEqual(rows[0]["quoted"], D("15.00"))

    def test_counting_order_is_stable(self):
        cat = parse_catalog(support.CATALOG)
        moves = parse_movements("2024-03-02 AB-100 +1 a\n2024-03-01 AB-100 +1 b\n2024-03-02 AB-100 +1 c\n", cat)
        self.assertEqual([m.note for m in counting_order(moves)], ["b", "a", "c"])

    def test_parse_error_fields(self):
        err = ParseError(7, "oops")
        self.assertEqual((err.line, err.reason, str(err)), (7, "oops", "line 7: oops"))


class MoneyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_money_half_up_and_no_negative_zero(self):
        self.assertEqual(money(D("0.005")), D("0.01"))
        self.assertEqual(money(D("-0.004")), D("0.00"))
        self.assertEqual(str(money(D("-0.00"))), "0.00")

    def test_fmt(self):
        self.assertEqual(fmt(D("-0")), "0.00")
        self.assertEqual(fmt(D("-7.5")), "-7.50")
        self.assertEqual(fmt(D("3")), "3.00")


class CliHelperTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_usage_error_and_exit(self):
        exc = cli.usage_error("no command given")
        self.assertIsInstance(exc, cli.Exit)
        self.assertEqual(exc.status, 2)
        self.assertTrue(exc.message.startswith("no command given\nusage:"))

    def test_args_defaults(self):
        args = cli.Args()
        self.assertEqual((args.command, args.dir, args.json, args.format, args.positionals),
                         (None, ".", False, "text", []))

    def test_parse_args(self):
        args = cli.parse_args(["--json", "history", "--dir", "x", "ab-100", "--dir=y"])
        self.assertEqual((args.command, args.dir, args.json, args.positionals), ("history", "y", True, ["ab-100"]))
        args = cli.parse_args(["receive", "2024-03-01", "AB-100", "-5", "--json"])
        self.assertEqual(args.positionals, ["2024-03-01", "AB-100", "-5", "--json"])
        for bad in (["stock", "--jso"], ["report", "--format=xml"], ["fulfil", "SO-1", "2024-02-30"]):
            with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
                cli.parse_args(bad)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 2)

    def test_files(self):
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
            cli.Files("/nonexistent/stockroom/dir")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 2)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            files = cli.Files(d)
            self.assertEqual(files.read_text("movements.txt"), "")
            with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit):
                files.read_text("catalog.txt", required=True)

    def test_to_json_and_lines_out(self):
        self.assertEqual(cli.to_json([{"a": "é"}]), '[\n  {\n    "a": "é"\n  }\n]\n')
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out(["a", "b"]), "a\nb\n")
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out([]), "")

    def test_known_sku_and_find_order(self):
        cat, _, orders = shop()
        self.assertEqual(cli.known_sku("cd-205", cat), "CD-205")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
            cli.known_sku("ZZ-999", cat)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 1)
        self.assertEqual(cli.find_order("so-1002", orders).id, "SO-1002")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit):
            cli.find_order("SO-01002", orders)

    def test_quote_output(self):
        cat, _, orders = shop()
        from stockroom import price_order

        q = price_order(orders[0], cat)
        self.assertEqual(cli.order_header(orders[0]), "SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme")
        text = cli.quote_output("invoice X", orders[0], q, False)
        self.assertTrue(text.startswith("invoice X\nAB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50\n"))
        data = json.loads(cli.quote_output("ignored", orders[0], q, True))
        self.assertEqual(data["lines"][0]["discount"], "-7.50")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

        for bad in (["stock", "--jso"], ["report", "--format=xml"], ["fulfil", "SO-1", "2024-02-30"]):
            with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
                cli.parse_args(bad)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 2)

    def test_files(self):
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
            cli.Files("/nonexistent/stockroom/dir")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 2)
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            files = cli.Files(d)
            self.assertEqual(files.read_text("movements.txt"), "")
            with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit):
                files.read_text("catalog.txt", required=True)

    def test_to_json_and_lines_out(self):
        self.assertEqual(cli.to_json([{"a": "é"}]), '[\n  {\n    "a": "é"\n  }\n]\n')
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out(["a", "b"]), "a\nb\n")
        self.assertEqual(cli.lines_out([]), "")

    def test_known_sku_and_find_order(self):
        cat, _, orders = shop()
        self.assertEqual(cli.known_sku("cd-205", cat), "CD-205")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit) as ctx:
            cli.known_sku("ZZ-999", cat)
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.status, 1)
        self.assertEqual(cli.find_order("so-1002", orders).id, "SO-1002")
        with self.assertRaises(cli.Exit):
            cli.find_order("SO-01002", orders)

    def test_quote_output(self):
        cat, _, orders = shop()
        from stockroom import price_order

        q = price_order(orders[0], cat)
        self.assertEqual(cli.order_header(orders[0]), "SO-1001 2024-03-03 acme")
        text = cli.quote_output("invoice X", orders[0], q, False)
        self.assertTrue(text.startswith("invoice X\nAB-100 12 12.50 150.00 -7.50 142.50\n"))

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# stockroom

A small, standard-library-only Python tool (Python 3.9 or newer) for a one-person shop that keeps its
catalogue, stock movements and customer orders in plain text files. It works both as a library
(`import stockroom`) and as a `stockroom` command.

## Install

    pip install .

## Files

All three live in one folder (the current folder, or the one given with `--dir DIR`):

- `catalog.txt` — `SKU | name | price | reorder [| tax]`, tax one of `standard`, `reduced`, `zero`.
- `movements.txt` — `DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]`, positive quantities in, negative out.
- `orders.txt` — `ORDER DATE CUSTOMER SKU*QTY,SKU*QTY,...`.

Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. Any mistake is reported with the file name and line number.

## Commands

    stockroom stock [--json]                    on-hand quantity and ok/low/out status
    stockroom low [--json]                      what to buy
    stockroom history SKU [--json]              a product's movements with running balance
    stockroom receive DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]  record stock coming in
    stockroom ship DATE SKU QUANTITY [NOTE]     record stock going out
    stockroom quote ORDER [--json]              price an order
    stockroom fulfil ORDER DATE                 ship what the shelves can cover
    stockroom invoice ORDER [--json]            bill what has shipped so far
    stockroom report [--format text|csv|json]   one row per order

Exit status is 0 on success, 1 for a mistake in a data file or a refused request, and 2 for an
unreadable file or a wrong command line.

## Library

```python
import stockroom

catalog = stockroom.parse_catalog(open("catalog.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())
moves = stockroom.parse_movements(open("movements.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
orders = stockroom.parse_orders(open("orders.txt", encoding="utf-8").read(), catalog)
print(stockroom.stock_levels(catalog, moves))
print(stockroom.price_order(orders[0], catalog).total)
```

A bad line raises `stockroom.ParseError` (a `ValueError`) whose `.line` is the line number.

## Tests

    python -m unittest discover -s tests
EOF

Implements PRD #1 (closes #2): the `stockroom` package, which is both an importable library and a `stockroom` console command. It uses only the standard library and needs Python 3.9 or newer.

## What is included

- `pyproject.toml` (setuptools, no dependencies) with the `stockroom = stockroom.cli:main` entry point, plus `python -m stockroom`.
- `parsing.py`: a shared line reader that strips the BOM and ends lines only at LF or CRLF (it never uses `splitlines`). It ignores blank lines and `#` comments, matches numbers against ASCII-only patterns, and provides `parse_catalog`, `parse_movements` (including the never-below-zero check in date order) and `parse_orders`. Errors are raised as `ParseError`, a `ValueError` with `.line`.
- `shelves.py`: stock levels, ok/low/out status, buy quantities and history.
- `pricing.py`: `price_order`, using `Decimal` with half-up rounding throughout. It covers the volume discount, the 3 % order discount at £500.00 or more, largest-remainder penny allocation (earlier line wins a tie) and per-line tax.
- `orders.py`: shipped-so-far, status, the fulfil availability rule (never breaks a later movement), invoices and report rows.
- `cli.py`: a hand-written argument parser. Options must be spelled in full, and `--dir` is accepted anywhere. It checks the command line first, then the files, then the request, and exits 0, 1 or 2. Output is built before anything is printed and written as UTF-8; `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` append in a single write and leave the file untouched when they refuse; a broken pipe exits 0 quietly.

## Tests

`python -m unittest discover -s tests` runs 82 tests, all passing on Python 3.13 and 3.9. The pip-install smoke test skips on 3.9 because that interpreter has no working pip.

The suite covers every parser rule and pitfall (`splitlines` characters, `1_000`, Unicode digits, BOM, CRLF), the SO-1001 worked example (148.47 / 28.80 / 177.27), orders over £500 with allocation and half-up rounding, and every command's text and JSON output. It also covers exit codes, a refused movement leaving the file byte-identical, the missing-final-newline case, and the broken pipe. To check that the tests catch real bugs, I made deliberate breaks one at a time and confirmed the suite fails for each: half-even rounding, removing the broken-pipe handler, using `splitlines`, dropping the later-movement cap in fulfil, and reversing the allocation tie-break.

## Decisions where the request is silent

- Error messages name the file by its bare name (for example `stockroom: movements.txt: line 4: bad date '2024-02-30'`).
- When `receive` or `ship` is refused because the new movement would make a later movement go below zero, the message names that later line.
- Options given before the command name (for example `stockroom --json stock`) are accepted for commands that take options. For `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil` they are rejected as unknown options.

content.text:
I built the `stockroom` library and command for PRD #1 and merged it as PR #3 (squash). The PR closes issue #2.

**What's in it:** `pip install .` gives you both `import stockroom` and the `stockroom` command, using only the standard library. The parts:
- Readers for `catalog.txt`, `movements.txt` and `orders.txt`. Every mistake is reported with the file name and line number.
- Stock levels and pricing: volume discounts, the 3 % order discount from £500, pennies of discount shared out by largest remainder, tax per line, all rounding halves up.
- All nine commands: `stock`, `low`, `history`, `receive`, `ship`, `quote`, `fulfil`, `invoice` and `report`.

The outputs match the examples in your request exactly, including SO-1001 (subtotal 148.47, tax 28.80, total 177.27).

**Testing:** the suite has 82 `unittest` tests. They pass on Python 3.13 and 3.9; on 3.9 the `pip install` test is skipped because that interpreter has no working pip, and it passes on 3.13. To check the tests catch real bugs, I broke the code on purpose five ways one at a time (wrong rounding, splitting lines the wrong way, letting `fulfil` break a later movement, flipping the tie-break when sharing out discount pennies, and removing the handling for `stockroom stock | head -1`). The suite failed each time.

rtdd can't see tests that run the command in a separate process, so I added direct tests for the order, pricing and command-line helpers. The only files it still listed as untested are `__init__.py`, `__main__.py`, `pyproject.toml` and other non-code files. The command-line tests and the install test exercise these, even though rtdd can't trace it. The repo has no local CI script, so the gate was rtdd's Rounds 1 and 2. I didn't run the gate again after adding the README, since that change is text only.

**Choices I made where your request is silent** (also listed in the PR):
- Error messages name the file by its bare name, e.g. `stockroom: movements.txt: line 4: bad date '2024-02-30'`.
- If `receive` or `ship` is refused because it would take a later movement below zero, the message names that later line.
- Options can come before the command (`stockroom --json stock`). For `receive`, `ship` and `fulfil`, anything dash-led before the command name is rejected with exit 2.

I found no conflicts between your request, the PRD and the issue.
